instructions: Trim the fennel and set a few of the feathery fronds aside. Halve the bulb and slice it as thinly as you can.
Cut the peel and white pith off the oranges and slice them into rounds. Roughly chop the olives.
In a small bowl, whisk 2 tablespoons of the olive oil with 1 tablespoon of lemon juice, 1 tablespoon of chopped parsley, the salt and the pepper.
Drizzle the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil over a platter. Arrange the fennel and orange slices on top, scatter over the olives and spoon the dressing over everything.
Top with the fennel fronds and serve at room temperature. Put the red pepper flakes on the table for the adults.
method_notes: Unpeeled Journal (the lead, 5.0 from 2 ratings, so a fallback lead) layers raw fennel and orange with olives and a lemon and olive oil dressing, and I scaled its amounts from 6 servings to 4. Tastefully Grace roasts the fennel first and adds honey, which takes 55 minutes and isn't the no-cook salad the list promises, so I left that out. Pick Up Limes was behind a paywall. The red pepper flakes are moved to the table so the salad stays mild.
